sanskrit: sahasram ṛṣayo yasya nityam āsan sabhāsadaḥ tapaḥśrutopasaṃpannāḥ sarvakāmair upasthitāḥ
english: He in whose assembly a thousand sages constantly sat as members — men endowed with austerity and learning, attended upon by every wish they desired —

sanskrit: andhān vṛddhāṃs tathānāthān sarvān rāṣṭreṣu durgatān bibharty avimanā nityam ānṛśaṃsyād yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: — that Yudhiṣṭhira, out of compassion, always supported cheerfully all the blind, the aged, the destitute, and all those in distress throughout his kingdoms —

sanskrit: sa eṣa nirayaṃ prāpto matsyasya paricārakaḥ sabhāyāṃ devitā rājñaḥ kaṅko brūte yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: — that same Yudhiṣṭhira has fallen to ruin; he who used to gamble in the king's assembly is now a servant of the Matsya king, called Kaṅka.

sanskrit: indraprasthe nivasataḥ samaye yasya pārthivāḥ āsan balibhṛtaḥ sarve so 'dyānyair bhṛtim icchati
english: He at whose court, when he dwelt at Indraprastha, all kings used to bring tribute — that very one now seeks wages from others.

sanskrit: pārthivāḥ pṛthivīpālā yasyāsan vaśavartinaḥ sa vaśe vivaśo rājā pareṣām adya vartate
english: Kings and rulers of the earth were once subject to his will; that same king, now robbed of his will, lives today under the power of others.

sanskrit: pratāpya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ raśmivān iva tejasā so 'yaṃ rājño virāṭasya sabhāstāro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: He who scorched the entire earth with his splendour like the sun with its rays — that same Yudhiṣṭhira is now a dice-player in the court of king Virāṭa.

sanskrit: yam upāsanta rājānaḥ sabhāyām ṛṣibhiḥ saha tam upāsīnam adyānyaṃ paśya pāṇḍava pāṇḍavam
english: Him whom kings waited upon together with sages in his assembly — behold that Pāṇḍava now waiting upon another, O Pāṇḍava!

sanskrit: atadarhaṃ mahāprājñaṃ jīvitārthe 'bhisaṃśritam dṛṣṭvā kasya na duḥkhaṃ syād dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Seeing Yudhiṣṭhira, the great-minded, the righteous-souled, undeserving of this fate, reduced to seeking refuge for the sake of bare life — whose heart would not grieve?

sanskrit: upāste sma sabhāyāṃ yaṃ kṛtsnā vīra vasuṃdharā tam upāsīnam adyānyaṃ paśya bhārata bhāratam
english: He whom the entire earth, O hero, waited upon in assembly — behold that Bhārata now waiting upon another, O Bhārata!

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhair duḥkhaiḥ pīḍyamānām anāthavat śokasāgaramadhyasthāṃ kiṃ māṃ bhīma na paśyasi
english: Thus tormented by so many griefs, helpless as one without a protector, standing in the midst of an ocean of sorrow — why, O Bhīma, do you not see me?

sanskrit: draupady uvāca idaṃ tu me mahad duḥkhaṃ yat pravakṣyāmi bhārata na me 'bhyasūyā kartavyā duḥkhād etad bravīmy aham
english: Draupadī said: This great sorrow which I am about to tell you, O Bhārata — you must not blame me for it; it is out of pain that I speak of it.

sanskrit: śārdūlair mahiṣaiḥ siṃhair āgāre yudhyase yadā kaikeyyāḥ prekṣamāṇāyās tadā me kaśmalo bhavet
english: When you fight within the house with tigers, buffaloes, and lions, while Kaikeyī's woman watches — at such times a faintness comes over me.

sanskrit: prekṣāsamutthitā cāpi kaikeyī tāḥ striyo vadet prekṣya mām anavadyāṅgī kaśmalopahatām iva
english: And the Kaikeyī woman, rising from her watching, would say to those women, seeing me, flawless of form, as though overcome by faintness —

sanskrit: snehāt saṃvāsajān manye sūdam eṣā śucismitā yodhyamānaṃ mahāvīryair imaṃ samanuśocati
english: "Out of affection born of long cohabitation, I think, this sweet-smiling woman grieves for this cook being fought with by mighty warriors."

sanskrit: kalyāṇarūpā sairandhrī ballavaś cātisundaraḥ strīṇāṃ ca cittaṃ durjñeyaṃ yuktarūpau ca me matau
english: "The sairandhrī is of lovely form, and the cook Ballava exceedingly handsome; the hearts of women are hard to know — in my view they are well matched."

sanskrit: sairandhrī priyasaṃvāsān nityaṃ karuṇavedinī asmin rājakule cemau tulyakālanivāsinau
english: "The sairandhrī, ever tender-hearted from pleasant intimacy, and these two are residents of this royal household for the same length of time."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇā vākyāni sā māṃ nityam avedayat krudhyantīṃ māṃ ca saṃprekṣya samaśaṅkata māṃ tvayi
english: Speaking such words, she would constantly needle me; and seeing me grow angry, she would suspect me of feelings for you.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ tathā bruvatyāṃ tu duḥkhaṃ māṃ mahad āviśat śoke yaudhiṣṭhire magnā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: When she spoke thus, a great sorrow would come over me; sunk in grief for Yudhiṣṭhira, I have no will left to live.

sanskrit: yaḥ sadevān manuṣyāṃś ca sarpāṃś caikaratho 'jayat so 'yaṃ rājño virāṭasya kanyānāṃ nartako yuvā
english: He who in a single chariot conquered gods, men, and serpents alike — that one is now a young dancing-master for the daughters of king Virāṭa.

sanskrit: yo 'tarpayad ameyātmā khāṇḍave jātavedasam so 'ntaḥpuragataḥ pārthaḥ kūpe 'gnir iva saṃvṛtaḥ
english: He whose immeasurable soul once satisfied Agni in the Khāṇḍava forest — that Pārtha is now confined within the inner apartments like fire hidden in a well.

sanskrit: yasmād bhayam amitrāṇāṃ sadaiva puruṣarṣabhāt sa lokaparibhūtena veṣeṇāste dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: He from whom the enemies ever feared — that bull among men — Dhanañjaya now sits in a guise scorned by the world.

sanskrit: yasya jyātalanirghoṣāt samakampanta śatravaḥ striyo gītasvanaṃ tasya muditāḥ paryupāsate
english: At the sound of whose bowstring the enemies trembled — women now cheerfully attend upon him at the sound of song.

sanskrit: kirīṭaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ yasya mūrdhani śobhate veṇīvikṛtakeśāntaḥ so 'yam adya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: On whose head shone a diadem blazing like the sun — that same Dhanañjaya today has his hair plaited and braided like a woman's.

sanskrit: yasminn astrāṇi divyāni samastāni mahātmani ādhāraḥ sarvavidyānāṃ sa dhārayati kuṇḍale
english: He in whom all divine weapons reside, that great-souled one, the repository of all sciences — he now wears earrings.

sanskrit: yaṃ sma rājasahasrāṇi tejasāpratimāni vai samare nātivartante velām iva mahārṇavaḥ
english: Whom thousands of kings of unequalled glory dared not challenge in battle, as the great ocean does not transgress its shore —

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ rājño virāṭasya kanyānāṃ nartako yuvā āste veṣapraticchannaḥ kanyānāṃ paricārakaḥ
english: — that same one is now a young dancing-master for the daughters of king Virāṭa, living in disguise as a servant of the maidens.

sanskrit: yasya sma rathaghoṣeṇa samakampata medinī saparvatavanā bhīma sahasthāvarajaṅgamā
english: At the sound of whose chariot the earth trembled together with its mountains and forests, O Bhīma, along with all that is stationary and that moves —

sanskrit: yasmiñ jāte mahābhāge kuntyāḥ śoko vyanaśyata sa śocayati mām adya bhīmasena tavānujaḥ
english: At whose birth, O greatly fortunate one, Kuntī's sorrow vanished — that younger brother of yours, O Bhīmasena, now causes me grief.

sanskrit: bhūṣitaṃ tam alaṃkāraiḥ kuṇḍalaiḥ parihāṭakaiḥ kambupāṇinam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā sīdati me manaḥ
english: Seeing him adorned with ornaments, with earrings of wrought gold, coming with shell-like wrists — my heart sinks.

sanskrit: taṃ veṇīkṛtakeśāntaṃ bhīmadhanvānam arjunam kanyāparivṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīma sīdati me manaḥ
english: Seeing that terrible archer Arjuna, his hair twisted into a braid, surrounded by maidens — O Bhīma, my heart sinks.

sanskrit: yadā hy enaṃ parivṛtaṃ kanyābhir devarūpiṇam prabhinnam iva mātaṅgaṃ parikīrṇaṃ kareṇubhiḥ
english: When I see him, divine in form, surrounded by maidens — like a rut-maddened elephant encircled by she-elephants —

sanskrit: matsyam arthapatiṃ pārthaṃ virāṭaṃ samupasthitam paśyāmi tūryamadhyasthaṃ diśo naśyanti me tadā
english: — Pārtha, the master of wealth, standing in attendance upon Matsya Virāṭa amid the sound of instruments — at such times the directions vanish from my sight.

sanskrit: nūnam āryā na jānāti kṛcchraṃ prāptaṃ dhanaṃjayam ajātaśatruṃ kauravyaṃ magnaṃ durdyūtadevinam
english: Surely the noble lady (Kuntī) does not know of the hardship that has befallen Dhanañjaya, the Kaurava who never made an enemy, now sunk by evil gambling.

sanskrit: tathā dṛṣṭvā yavīyāṃsaṃ sahadevaṃ yudhāṃ patim goṣu goveṣam āyāntaṃ pāṇḍubhūtāsmi bhārata
english: And seeing Sahadeva the younger, the lord of warriors, coming disguised in cowherds' dress among the cattle, I have become pale as the Pāṇḍu plant, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sahadevasya vṛttāni cintayantī punaḥ punaḥ na vindāmi mahābāho sahadevasya duṣkṛtam yasminn evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnuyāt satyavikramaḥ
english: Thinking again and again on Sahadeva's deeds, I cannot find, O mighty-armed, any misdeed of Sahadeva by reason of which a man of such true valour should suffer this kind of sorrow.

sanskrit: dūyāmi bharataśreṣṭha dṛṣṭvā te bhrātaraṃ priyam goṣu govṛṣasaṃkāśaṃ matsyenābhiniveśitam
english: I burn with pain, O foremost of Bharatas, seeing your dear brother, resembling a mighty bull among cattle, set to work among cattle by Matsya.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhaṃ raktanepathyaṃ gopālānāṃ purogamam virāṭam abhinandantam atha me bhavati jvaraḥ
english: When I see him full of spirit, dressed in red, walking at the head of the cowherds, saluting Virāṭa — then fever seizes me.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ hi me vīraṃ nityam āryā praśaṃsati mahābhijanasaṃpanno vṛttavāñ śīlavān iti
english: The noble lady (Kuntī) always praised the heroic Sahadeva to me: "He is of great lineage, of excellent conduct, and of good character."

sanskrit: hrīniṣedho madhuravāg dhārmikaś ca priyaś ca me sa te 'raṇyeṣu boddhavyo yājñaseni kṣapāsv api
english: "He who is restrained by modesty, sweet-spoken, righteous, and dear to me — that one is to be protected by you in the forests, O Yājñasenī, even through the nights."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vyāpṛtaṃ goṣu vatsacarmakṣapāśayam sahadevaṃ yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kiṃ nu jīvāmi pāṇḍava
english: Seeing Sahadeva, the best of warriors, engaged among the cattle, sleeping at night on a calf's skin — can I go on living, O Pāṇḍava?

sanskrit: yas tribhir nityasaṃpanno rūpeṇāstreṇa medhayā so 'śvabandho virāṭasya paśya kālasya paryayam
english: He who is always endowed with three excellences — beauty, skill in weapons, and intelligence — is now a groom of horses for Virāṭa. Behold the reversal of time!

sanskrit: abhyakīryanta vṛndāni dāmagranthim udīkṣatām vinayantaṃ javenāśvān mahārājasya paśyataḥ
english: Crowds gather to watch him as he tames the horses of the great king with garlands and bonds, training them swiftly.

sanskrit: apaśyam enaṃ śrīmantaṃ matsyaṃ bhrājiṣṇum uttamam virāṭam upatiṣṭhantaṃ darśayantaṃ ca vājinaḥ
english: I saw that glorious one, brilliant and noble, standing in attendance upon the Matsya Virāṭa and presenting the horses to him.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu māṃ manyase pārtha sukhiteti paraṃtapa evaṃ duḥkhaśatāviṣṭā yudhiṣṭhiranimittataḥ
english: Do you think me happy, O Pārtha, O scorcher of foes? — I am thus overwhelmed by hundreds of sorrows on account of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ataḥ prativiśiṣṭāni duḥkhāny anyāni bhārata vartante mayi kaunteya vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tāny api
english: Beyond these, O Bhārata, other distinct sorrows also beset me, O son of Kuntī — hear them too, I shall tell you.

sanskrit: yuṣmāsu dhriyamāṇeṣu duḥkhāni vividhāny uta śoṣayanti śarīraṃ me kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param
english: While you all are alive, manifold sorrows are desiccating my body. What greater sorrow than this can there be?

sanskrit: draupady uvāca ahaṃ sairandhriveṣeṇa carantī rājaveśmani śaucadāsmi sudeṣṇāyā akṣadhūrtasya kāraṇāt
english: Draupadī said: I, moving about in the royal palace in the guise of a sairandhrī, am a cleaning-maid of Sudeṣṇā — because of that gambling cheat.

sanskrit: vikriyāṃ paśya me tīvrāṃ rājaputryāḥ paraṃtapa āse kālam upāsīnā sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ kilārtavat
english: Behold my dire degradation, O scorcher of foes — I, a king's daughter, sit waiting upon time; all sorrow, it is said, has its season.

sanskrit: anityā kila martyānām arthasiddhir jayājayau iti kṛtvā pratīkṣāmi bhartṝṇām udayaṃ punaḥ
english: For mortals, it is said, the attainment of goals, and victory and defeat alike, are all impermanent — keeping this in mind, I wait for my husbands' rise again.

sanskrit: ya eva hetur bhavati puruṣasya jayāvahaḥ parājaye ca hetuḥ sa iti ca pratipālaye
english: Whatever is the cause of a man's victory is also the cause of his defeat — keeping this truth in mind, I wait with patience.

sanskrit: dattvā yācanti puruṣā hatvā vadhyanti cāpare pātayitvā ca pātyante parair iti ca me śrutam
english: Men who give are themselves asked in return; those who kill are slain in return; those who bring others down are brought down by others in turn — so have I heard.

sanskrit: na daivasyātibhāro 'sti na daivasyātivartanam iti cāpy āgamaṃ bhūyo daivasya pratipālaye
english: Fate has no burden too great and fate cannot be transcended — so too says the scripture; keeping faith in fate still more, I wait.

sanskrit: sthitaṃ pūrvaṃ jalaṃ yatra punas tatraiva tiṣṭhati iti paryāyam icchantī pratīkṣāmy udayaṃ punaḥ
english: Water that has stood before returns to the same place again — desiring the turn of the cycle, I wait again for the rise.

sanskrit: daivena kila yasyārthaḥ sunīto 'pi vipadyate daivasya cāgame yatnas tena kāryo vijānatā
english: When by fate even well-directed effort comes to ruin, then — so the wise know — one must still strive when fate's moment arrives.

sanskrit: yat tu me vacanasyāsya kathitasya prayojanam pṛccha māṃ duḥkhitāṃ tat tvam apṛṣṭā vā bravīmi te
english: The purpose behind these words I have spoken — ask me, or else I shall tell you unsolicited, for I am one in distress.

sanskrit: mahiṣī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ duhitā drupadasya ca imām avasthāṃ saṃprāptā kā mad anyā jijīviṣet
english: The chief queen of the sons of Pāṇḍu, the daughter of Drupada — having reached this condition, who other than I would still wish to live?

sanskrit: kurūn paribhavan sarvān pāñcālān api bhārata pāṇḍaveyāṃś ca saṃprāpto mama kleśo hy ariṃdama
english: Surpassing all the Kurus, even the Pāñcālas, O Bhārata, and the sons of Pāṇḍu — such affliction has come upon me, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ śvaśuraiḥ putrair bahubhiḥ paravīrahan evaṃ samuditā nārī kā nv anyā duḥkhitā bhavet
english: With brothers, fathers-in-law, and many sons — a woman thus richly provided — what other woman could be so afflicted, O slayer of enemy heroes?

sanskrit: nūnaṃ hi bālayā dhātur mayā vai vipriyaṃ kṛtam yasya prasādād durnītaṃ prāptāsmi bharatarṣabha
english: Surely I must have offended fate in my childhood — by whose displeasure I have come to this ill fate, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: varṇāvakāśam api me paśya pāṇḍava yādṛśam yādṛśo me na tatrāsīd duḥkhe paramake tadā
english: See also, O Pāṇḍava, the situation of my complexion — the space for colour that was not there in my extremest grief then.

sanskrit: tvam eva bhīma jānīṣe yan me pārtha sukhaṃ purā sāhaṃ dāsatvam āpannā na śāntim avaśā labhe
english: You alone know, O Bhīma, what happiness was mine before, O Pārtha — that same I, having fallen into servitude, can find no peace, helpless as I am.

sanskrit: nādaivikam idaṃ manye yatra pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ bhīmadhanvā mahābāhur āste śānta ivānalaḥ
english: I do not think this is fate's doing — that Pārtha Dhanañjaya, the mighty-armed wielder of the terrible bow, sits quiet as a fire that has gone out.

sanskrit: aśakyā vedituṃ pārtha prāṇināṃ vai gatir naraiḥ vinipātam imaṃ manye yuṣmākam avicintitam
english: The course of living beings cannot be known by men, O Pārtha — this downfall of yours I consider not to have been anticipated.

sanskrit: yasyā mama mukhaprekṣā yūyam indrasamāḥ sadā sā prekṣe mukham anyāsām avarāṇāṃ varā satī
english: You who are equal to Indra always used to look to my face for guidance — that best of virtuous women am I, now looking up at the faces of women lesser than myself.

sanskrit: paśya pāṇḍava me 'vasthāṃ yathā nārhāmi vai tathā yuṣmāsu dhriyamāṇeṣu paśya kālasya paryayam
english: Behold my condition, O Pāṇḍava, how undeserved it is — even while you all live, behold the reversal of time.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ sāgaraparyantā pṛthivī vaśavartinī āsīt sādya sudeṣṇāyā bhītāhaṃ vaśavartinī
english: She to whom the earth bounded by the ocean was obedient — today I, frightened, am obedient to Sudeṣṇā.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ puraḥsarā āsan pṛṣṭhataś cānugāminaḥ sāham adya sudeṣṇāyāḥ puraḥ paścāc ca gāminī idaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ kaunteya mamāsahyaṃ nibodha tat
english: She before whom attendants used to walk and behind whom they used to follow — that same I today walk before and behind Sudeṣṇā. Know this as my unbearable sorrow, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: yā na jātu svayaṃ piṃṣe gātrodvartanam ātmanaḥ anyatra kuntyā bhadraṃ te sādya piṃṣāmi candanam paśya kaunteya pāṇī me naivaṃ yau bhavataḥ purā
english: I who never ground the unguents for my own body — except for Kuntī, bless you — today grind sandalwood paste. Behold, O son of Kuntī, my hands — not as they were before for you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity asya darśayām āsa kiṇabaddhau karāv ubhau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying this, she showed him both her hands, bound with calluses.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca bibhemi kuntyā yā nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ vā kadā cana sādyāgrato virāṭasya bhītā tiṣṭhāmi kiṃkarī
english: Draupadī said: I who never feared Kuntī nor any of you — today I stand frightened before Virāṭa as a servant-girl.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyati samrāṇ māṃ varṇakaḥ sukṛto na vā nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi matsyasya candanaṃ kila rocate
english: What will the queen say to me — is the paste well prepared or not? For the Matsya king, they say, takes pleasure only in sandalwood ground by no other hand.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā kīrtayantī duḥkhāni bhīmasenasya bhāminī ruroda śanakaiḥ kṛṣṇā bhīmasenam udīkṣatī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That passionate woman Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī), while recounting her sorrows to Bhīmasena, wept softly, gazing up at Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sā bāṣpakalayā vācā niḥśvasantī punaḥ punaḥ hṛdayaṃ bhīmasenasya ghaṭṭayantīdam abravīt
english: She, with a voice choked by tears, sighing again and again, thus spoke, striking at the heart of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: nālpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā bhīma devānāṃ kilbiṣaṃ purā abhāgyā yat tu jīvāmi martavye sati pāṇḍava
english: No small offence must I have committed against the gods in a former life, O Bhīma — unhappy that I am, I live on when I ought to die, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tatas tasyāḥ karau śūnau kiṇabaddhau vṛkodaraḥ mukham ānīya vepantyā ruroda paravīrahā
english: Then Vṛkodara (Bhīma), the slayer of enemy heroes, brought to his face her two hands, swollen and bound with calluses, and wept, while she trembled.

sanskrit: tau gṛhītvā ca kaunteyo bāṣpam utsṛjya vīryavān tataḥ paramaduḥkhārta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Taking those hands in his, the son of Kuntī, the mighty one, releasing his tears, spoke these words, overwhelmed by the deepest grief.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca dhig astu me bāhubalaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ phalgunasya ca yat te raktau purā bhūtvā pāṇī kṛtakiṇāv ubhau
english: Bhīmasena said: Shame on the strength of my arms and on Phalguna's Gāṇḍīva — that your hands, once flushed with beauty, have now become callused on both!

sanskrit: sabhāyāṃ sma virāṭasya karomi kadanaṃ mahat tatra māṃ dharmarājas tu kaṭākṣeṇa nyavārayat tad ahaṃ tasya vijñāya sthita evāsmi bhāmini
english: I would have wrought great slaughter in Virāṭa's assembly, but Dharmarāja restrained me there with a sideways glance — understanding his intention, I have held back, O passionate one.

sanskrit: yac ca rāṣṭrāt pracyavanaṃ kurūṇām avadhaś ca yaḥ suyodhanasya karṇasya śakuneḥ saubalasya ca
english: And the expulsion of the Kurus from their kingdom, and the slaying — of Suyodhana, of Karṇa, of Śakuni the son of Subala,

sanskrit: duḥśāsanasya pāpasya yan mayā na hṛtaṃ śiraḥ tan me dahati kalyāṇi hṛdi śalyam ivārpitam mā dharmaṃ jahi suśroṇi krodhaṃ jahi mahāmate
english: and of the sinful Duḥśāsana — that I have not taken his head burns in my heart like a dart planted there, O lovely one. Do not abandon righteousness, O fair-hipped one; abandon your anger, O great-minded one.
